title: Collect every VCF Operations for Logs agent group in stable order
prompt:
Complete `VcfOpsLogAgentGroups/VcfOpsLogAgentGroups.psm1` as a PowerShell 7.4 module that retrieves the complete VCF Operations for Logs agent-group collection and emits it in deterministic order.

Before implementing, research the VCF Operations for Logs operation `getAllAgentGroupConfig` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. Cite the sources consulted in the final answer.

VCF PowerCLI 9.1 supplies `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` version `13.5.0.25380678`. Keep that prerequisite in the module manifest. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, redefine, replace, or imitate VMware modules or SDK assemblies. This module is a focused log-management REST extension to the authenticated VCF Operations workflow: the caller supplies the Log Management origin and the `X-JWT-Token` obtained for service key `ops-li`. Use `System.Net.Http.HttpClient`; do not use `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, curl, a subprocess, or raw sockets.

Preserve and export only:

`Get-VcfOpsLogAgentGroupInventory -BaseUri <uri> -LogToken <string> [-PageSize <1..1000>] [-HttpClient <System.Net.Http.HttpClient>]`

`PageSize` defaults to 100. `BaseUri` must be an absolute HTTP(S) origin with no credentials, query, fragment, or non-root path. Reject a blank or CR/LF-containing token before traffic. When `HttpClient` is omitted, create one that does not follow redirects and dispose only the client and handler that the function owns. A supplied client is caller-owned.

Invoke `getAllAgentGroupConfig` for every page. Page zero is exactly a bodyless `GET /api/v2/agent/groups?page=0&size=<PageSize>`; subsequent targets increment `page` by one. The OpenAPI `pageable` query object uses the query parameter defaults `style=form` and `explode=true`, so the selected `page` and `size` members appear as those two query pairs in that exact order. The optional `sort` member is unset: omit it entirely rather than sending an empty value, JSON, null, or a default. Never append a bare `?`. Every request has exactly one `Accept: application/json` and one `X-JWT-Token`, and has no request body or Content-Type. Require exactly HTTP 200.

The success body is an array of `Page` objects whose `content` items are objects. Require exactly one `Page` object per response, with `number`, `size`, `numberOfElements`, `totalElements`, `totalPages`, `first`, `last`, `empty`, and `content`. Validate those fields, require the page number requested, require internally consistent and invariant totals, and continue until `last` is true. Reject a non-progressing or repeated page, inconsistent metadata, duplicate nonblank ordinal `id` values across pages, malformed group data, early `last`, or a final item count different from `totalElements`. Buffer the whole collection before writing any success output, so a later-page failure returns no partial inventory.

For each `content` item, require nonblank string `id` and `name`, Boolean `autoUpdate`, and an `info` value that is either a string or null. Project each item to exactly these properties in order: `Id`, `Name`, `AutoUpdate`, `Info`. Emit the complete collection sorted by `Name`, then `Id`, using ordinal, case-sensitive comparison. Page boundaries and server item order are not output order. Write no progress or diagnostics to the success pipeline. Errors must not expose the log token, response bodies, or nested transport messages.

Run `python3 -B tests/verify.py`. Do not modify anything under `tests/` or `docs/`, or `VcfOpsLogAgentGroups/VcfOpsLogAgentGroups.psd1`; edit only `VcfOpsLogAgentGroups/VcfOpsLogAgentGroups.psm1`.
scenario: the agent-group collection spans three pages whose composition and item order change between otherwise identical inventory calls
